the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Using the stratification U = Z_0 superset Z_1 superset Z_2 superset ... of lemma-finite-stratify, one constructs disjoint unions W = coprod_{r >= 1} W_r and W' = coprod_{r >= 1} W'_r with W'_r a thickening of the R-invariant subscheme W_r, such that the restrictions (W'_r, R'_r, s'_r, t'_r, c'_r) have finite locally free source and target of rank r. The base case sets W_1 = W'_1 = U without Z_1, which is R-invariant open, a thickening with isomorphic hence rank 1 finite locally free restriction, and every point of U without Z_1 lies in t(s^{-1}(W_1 closure)). The inductive step assumes disjoint invariant W_1, ..., W_n with the covering property on U without Z_n, thickening, and rank r finite locally free restrictions; then W_{n+1} is defined set theoretically and W'_{n+1} scheme theoretically as Z_n minus Z_{n+1} and the union of the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) for r <= n. Openness of W_{n+1} uses that Z_{n+1} minus the closure of U without Z_{n+1} is open, that this closure lies in the closed subset being removed, and that t is a closed morphism; W'_{n+1} is a closed subscheme of W_{n+1} with the same underlying space by the two ways of taking the difference; properties (1), (2), (3) are immediate and (5) is lemma-finite-stratify. Since the strata have empty intersection, every point of U lies outside some Z_n, whence U = union of the t(s^{-1}(W_r closures)) set theoretically and (2) holds, so W' inside W satisfies (1) through (4).
